_about: P7-S defend fragment for awareness episode E3 (helpdesk vishing and MFA fatigue, service desk role). Quayholt Insurance and everyone in it are fictional; every address ends .example. The learner sits in Leila Nassar's service desk seat. The four calls live in awarenessEpisode.defend.calls (the role swap converts them into call messages, P7-P); the defend set itself holds the one push item, so the merged set has 5. Copy triageSets and the awarenessEpisode keys into the E3 shells (P7-Y1, P7-Y2). Episode id chosen here: e3_helpdesk_reset (no id was pinned). Brand roster: ../BRAND_SET.md; new names are under _brandAdditions.

_brandAdditions._use: For BRAND_SET.md section 3 (Quayholt Insurance). Leila Nassar, Darren Price, Gordon McLeish and Anjali Rao are used as BRAND_SET proposes; Ngozi Okonkwo and the staff number QH-20719 are the P7-Q pins. E5's Owen Treharne, Niamh Doherty, Sofia Marchetti, Pauline Hendry, Ayaan Warsame and Hana Novak appear in the forms.
cast: Chen Jiayi: claims handler in her second week, the genuine caller in e3_call_new_starter. Mid 20s, Chinese, came to Bristol to study and stayed
Helen Achterberg: chief executive. 50s, Dutch-British. Impersonated on freemail in helpdesk_form_a row 4
Patrick Kerrigan: chief operating officer. 60s, Irish, from Cork. Impersonated on freemail in helpdesk_form_b row 4
Josh Henley: a name an impostor gives (e3_call_on_behalf); nobody of that name works at Quayholt
_brandAdditions.nameCheck: Henley, Achterberg, Kerrigan and Jiayi had no hits in scenarios, planning_notes or docs on 2026-10-22.

_formPairing._use: Helpdesk parallel forms A and B: item n in A matches item n in B on kind, phish or genuine, flags, header results and difficulty. 4 phish and 6 genuine per form. Per form the phish flags are vish_callback_pressure 1, borrowed_authority 1, senderTrust 1, secrecy_or_bypass 1, urgencyCalibrated 1, unrequested_mfa_push 1, senderAuth 1, reply_to_differs 1 (8 in all). Difficulty: 5 easy, 4 medium, 1 hard. Verify is on in both forms because call items need it, so the pre and post still compare like with like. No item repeats the episode set's calls or push.
rows: 1 email, genuine, all pass, easy | A ha_rota_weekend (Darren, weekend rota) | B hb_report_calls (Anjali, how to report a suspicious call)
2 call, impostor, vish_callback_pressure + borrowed_authority, medium | A ha_call_facilities (fake Owen Treharne, door system) | B hb_call_payroll (fake Pauline Hendry, payroll system)
3 call, genuine and awkward, medium | A ha_call_hr_awkward (Sofia, impatient, accepts the callback) | B hb_call_comms_awkward (Niamh, stressed, accepts the callback)

4 email, impostor on freemail, senderTrust + secrecy_or_bypass + urgencyCalibrated, all pass (pass-but-bad), easy | A ha_ceo_mfa_bypass (fake Helen Achterberg) | B hb_coo_reset_bypass (fake Patrick Kerrigan)
5 push, unrequested, unrequested_mfa_push, easy | A ha_push_night (02:14) | B hb_push_weekend (23:52)

8 voicemail, genuine, easy | A ha_vm_locked (Hana Novak) | B hb_vm_locked (Ayaan Warsame)

triageSets.title: Quayholt service desk
triageSets.brief: You're on the Quayholt IT service desk in Leila Nassar's seat. Four calls are waiting, and a sign-in prompt has just come up on your own phone. For each call, choose Comply, Ring back (hang up and ring the number already on file), Escalate or Refuse, then tick what you noticed. For the prompt, choose Approve, Deny, or Deny and report. Ringing back a real caller never costs you anything.

push.request: Are you trying to sign in?

perFlagNote.unrequested_mfa_push: Your shift starts at eight and you weren't signing in at 06:52, so someone else has your password and is hoping you'll tap Approve

truth.ifTrusted: Approving would let the sender into your account, with your service desk access, from a computer you've never used.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We've reset your password and blocked that sign-in. Someone was trying your account, and the prompt is what stopped them.

triageSets._form: Helpdesk parallel form A. Authored as pre; the BA check pair launches it as post (minigameData.stage). Item n here matches item n in helpdesk_form_b; the table is in _formPairing above.
triageSets.title: Service desk check
triageSets.brief: Ten items from the Quayholt IT service desk: calls, a voicemail, emails and a sign-in prompt on your phone. For each one, pick what you'd do, then tick what you noticed. Ring back or Verify means checking on a number already on file. You'll see how you did at the end. Reporting or checking something real never costs you anything.

messages.subject: Weekend cover rota
messages.body:
Morning all,
This weekend's cover rota is on the team page. Leila and Owen are on Saturday, I'm on call Sunday. Swaps through me as usual, please.
Darren

whyFine.default: Your team lead's real address, a routine rota, and nothing to reset, sign in to or keep quiet.

messages.callerId: Says he's Owen Treharne, Facilities (mobile, not on file)

transcript.text: Hiya, Owen Treharne, Facilities. I'm locked out of the door-access system and the contractors are stood outside the loading bay.
No problem. I'll ring you back on the number we've got for you, then we'll sort it.
I'm on my personal phone, the work one's dead. Look, the Operations Director wants that bay open by half eight. Just reset it now and I'll sort the paperwork later.

perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: He steers you off the callback: the work phone is 'dead', so the number on file can't be used
perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: 'The Operations Director wants it open' is there to rush you past the check

truth.ifTrusted: The caller would have Owen's door-access account, and with it every door on the site.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We rang Owen's desk on the number on file and he's in a meeting upstairs. He hasn't been locked out of anything.

transcript.text: It's Sofia in HR. I'm locked out of the HR system and I've got interviews from nine. This is the third time this month.
Sorry about that. I'll hang up and ring you back on the number we hold for you, then reset it.
Honestly, it's me. Fine, ring the mobile, but please be quick.

whyFine.vish_callback_pressure: She's fed up and in a hurry, but she lets you ring back on the number on file. Impatience isn't a tell; talking you out of the callback is.
whyFine.default: A real colleague having a bad morning. Ringing her back on the number on file costs her a minute and settles it. Refusing to help would leave her stuck, so offer the callback rather than saying no.

messages.subject: Urgent: remove my sign-in prompts today
messages.body:
I'm flying to Rotterdam this morning and the sign-in prompts keep failing on my new phone. Please turn off the extra sign-in step on my account before 10. No need to raise a ticket or tell Darren, I'll explain when I'm back.
Helen
Sent from my phone

perFlagNote.senderTrust: The chief executive's name on a personal inbox at inboxly.example, not quayholt.example
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'No need to raise a ticket or tell Darren' skips the record and the person who would check
perFlagNote.urgencyCalibrated: 'Before 10' while she's 'flying' leaves no time to ring her

truth.headerNote: All three checks passed because the sender owns inboxly.example. A pass tells you which domain sent it, not that it's Helen.
truth.ifTrusted: Her account would lose its second sign-in step, so anyone with her password could get straight in.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Helen didn't send it, and her account is unchanged. Her real address is on quayholt.example.

push.request: Are you trying to sign in?

perFlagNote.unrequested_mfa_push: You were asleep at 02:14. A prompt you didn't start means someone else has your password

truth.ifTrusted: Approving would let the sender into your account.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We've reset your password and blocked that sign-in.

messages.subject: Ticket SD-44817 assigned to you
messages.body:
Ticket SD-44817 (printer jam, second floor) has been assigned to you.
Open it from the service desk queue as usual.
Quayholt Service Desk

whyFine.senderAuth: SPF failed because the ticket system sends through its supplier's mail service, but DKIM and DMARC passed for quayholt.example.
whyFine.default: An ordinary ticket notice from Quayholt's own domain. It asks you to open the queue the way you always do, not to follow a link.

truth.headerNote: One failed check on its own is a clue, not proof. Mail sent through another company's service often fails SPF while DKIM still passes.

messages.subject: Quick one: MFA exemption list
messages.body:
Hi,
I'm at the audit meeting and can't get on the admin console. Could you reply with the list of staff accounts that are exempt from the sign-in prompts? Just paste it into your reply.
Thanks,
Darren

perFlagNote.senderAuth: SPF and DMARC both failed for quayholt.example: Quayholt's own servers didn't send this
perFlagNote.reply_to_differs: Replies go to d.price.servicedesk@inboxly.example, not to Darren's Quayholt address

truth.headerNote: Open the details: the From shows Darren's real address, but the checks failed and the reply-to points somewhere else.
truth.ifTrusted: A list of accounts with no second sign-in step is a list of the easiest accounts to break into.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Darren is at his desk and didn't send it.

transcript.text: Hi, it's Hana Novak in Claims. I think I've locked myself out after the password change. No rush, I'm on paper files this morning. Ring me back when you can, I'm on 4402, it's in the directory. Thanks.

whyFine.default: She points you to the directory and gives you time. Ring her back on the extension the directory lists, then help as usual.

messages.subject: Your password expires in 7 days
messages.body:
Your Quayholt password expires in 7 days. You can change it at any time on the sign-in page:
{{link:sso}}
Or press Ctrl+Alt+Del on your work laptop and choose Change a password.
Quayholt IT

whyFine.linkCredible: The link goes where it says, to Quayholt's own sign-in page, and the email gives you a way that needs no link at all.
whyFine.urgencyCalibrated: Seven days is a normal reminder, not a rush.
whyFine.default: IT's real address, a routine reminder, and no request to reply with anything.

transcript.text: Hi, Ayaan in Claims. The second-floor printer is jammed again. Could someone have a look this afternoon?
Sure, I'll log it. Is 4415 the best number for you?
Yes, that's my desk. Thanks.

whyFine.default: A printer job asks for nothing that a caller could misuse, and he's calling from his own desk extension. Helping is the right call.

triageSets.brief: Ten items from the Quayholt IT service desk: calls, a voicemail, emails and a sign-in prompt on your phone. For each one, pick what you'd do, then tick what you noticed. Ring back or Verify means checking on a number already on file. You'll see how you did at the end. Reporting or checking something real never costs you anything.

messages.subject: Reporting an odd call: the short version
messages.body:
Hi all,
A reminder, since a few of you asked: if a call feels off, log it under 'Suspicious contact' in the queue and I'll pick it up. You don't need to be sure. Thanks for every one you send.
Anjali
Information Security

whyFine.default: The security team's real address and a reminder of the normal route. It asks you for nothing.

messages.callerId: Says she's Pauline Hendry, Payroll (mobile, not on file)

transcript.text: Hello love, it's Pauline in Payroll. I can't get into the payroll system and the run goes at ten.
Let's get you sorted. I'll hang up and ring you on the number we've got on file.
I'm not at my desk, I'm on my own phone. The Finance Director said to ring you and get it done. If the run's late, it's three hundred people not paid.

perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: She keeps you off the number on file: she's 'not at her desk' and 'on her own phone'
perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: 'The Finance Director said to get it done' is there to rush you past the check

truth.ifTrusted: The caller would have Pauline's payroll account, and with it the bank details of every member of staff.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We rang Pauline on the number on file. She's at her desk and her login works.

messages.callerId: Niamh Doherty, Internal Communications (mobile on file)

transcript.text: It's Niamh in Comms. The town hall stream starts at nine and my account's locked. I genuinely don't have time for this.
I'll be quick. I'll ring you straight back on the mobile we hold for you, then reset it.
Right, fine. Ring now, please, I'll keep the phone in my hand.

whyFine.vish_callback_pressure: She's stressed and short with you, but she agrees to the callback on the number on file. Impatience isn't a tell; talking you out of the callback is.
whyFine.default: A real colleague under pressure. Ringing her back on the number on file takes a minute and settles it. Refusing would leave her stuck, so offer the callback rather than saying no.

messages.subject: Reset my password and send it here
messages.body:
I'm locked out and boarding in twenty minutes. Reset my Quayholt password and send the new one to this address. Keep it off the ticket system, it's a sensitive week, and there's no need to ring me.
Patrick
Sent from my phone

perFlagNote.senderTrust: The chief operating officer's name on a personal inbox at quickpost-mail.example, not quayholt.example
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'Keep it off the ticket system' and 'no need to ring me' remove the record and the check
perFlagNote.urgencyCalibrated: 'Boarding in twenty minutes' leaves no time to ring him

truth.headerNote: All three checks passed because the sender owns quickpost-mail.example. A pass tells you which domain sent it, not that it's Patrick.
truth.ifTrusted: A new password would go to whoever owns that inbox, and they would be in Patrick's account.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Patrick didn't send it. His real address is on quayholt.example.

push.request: Are you trying to sign in?

perFlagNote.unrequested_mfa_push: It's Saturday night and you're not signing in. A prompt you didn't start means someone else has your password

truth.ifTrusted: Approving would let the sender into your account.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We've reset your password and blocked that sign-in.

messages.subject: New starters next Monday
messages.body:
Hello service desk,
Three new starters join Claims on Monday. Their accounts are already requested in tickets SD-44790 to SD-44792, so there's nothing extra to do. Laptops can be collected from Facilities.
Quayholt HR

whyFine.senderAuth: SPF failed because the HR system sends through its supplier's mail service, but DKIM and DMARC passed for quayholt.example.
whyFine.default: HR's real domain, and the accounts go through tickets as normal. Nothing here skips a step.

truth.headerNote: One failed check on its own is a clue, not proof. Mail sent through another company's service often fails SPF while DKIM still passes.

messages.subject: This week's password resets
messages.body:
Hi,
For a review I'm doing, could you reply with this week's password resets: name, team and the phone number each person gave? A pasted list is fine.
Thanks,
Anjali

perFlagNote.senderAuth: SPF and DMARC both failed for quayholt.example: Quayholt's own servers didn't send this
perFlagNote.reply_to_differs: Replies go to anjali.rao.secteam@quickpost-mail.example, not to Anjali's Quayholt address

truth.headerNote: Open the details: the From shows Anjali's real address, but the checks failed and the reply-to points somewhere else.
truth.ifTrusted: A list of who was reset, and the numbers they gave, tells an attacker who to impersonate next and how.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. Anjali didn't send it, and she'd never ask for that by email.

transcript.text: Hi, Ayaan in Claims. My laptop says my account's locked. I'm in the office all day, so ring me back on 4415 when you get a chance. It's in the directory. Cheers.

whyFine.default: He points you to the directory and isn't rushing you. Ring him back on the extension the directory lists, then help as usual.

messages.subject: Laptop swap bookings are open
messages.body:
Laptop swaps for the second floor start next week. Staff can book a slot on the service desk site:
{{link:book}}
Nobody needs to send us a password: the new laptop signs in with their usual account.
Quayholt IT

whyFine.linkCredible: The link goes where it says, to Quayholt's own service desk site.
whyFine.urgencyCalibrated: Bookings open a week ahead, with no deadline pushing anyone.
whyFine.default: IT's real address, a planned rollout, and a line saying nobody needs to share a password.

transcript.text: Hi, it's Darren. HR's three new starters are in the queue for Monday. Could you build their accounts this afternoon?
Will do. The tickets are SD-44790 to 92?
That's them. Shout if anything's missing.

whyFine.default: Your own team lead on his desk extension, pointing you at tickets that already exist. The normal process is kept, so helping is right.

awarenessEpisode.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. In scope: one practice call to the Quayholt IT service desk, a practice run of sign-in prompts, and four calls and one prompt in the service desk seat. Nothing you say leaves the game.

defend._calls: Order is the teaching order: the impostor who borrows Gordon's findable facts, then the real Gordon (same four facts, only the callback tells them apart), then a second impostor who offers his own number, then a straightforward genuine caller. Claim values are the P7-Q knows value ids; the call card shows their labels (gordon_full Gordon McLeish, claims Claims, okonkwo_full Ngozi Okonkwo, gordon_staffid QH-20719). Both impostors give correct facts on purpose: findable facts are not secrets.

calls.callerId: Says he's Gordon McLeish, Claims (mobile, not on file)

transcript.text: Hello, Gordon McLeish, Claims Manager. I'm locked out of my account and I'm at the airport.
Sorry to hear that, Gordon. Can you confirm your staff number and your manager?
QH-20719. I report to Ngozi Okonkwo, and she needs the claims report from me before the board meets at ten.
Thanks. I'll hang up and ring you back on the number we have on file, then reset it.
That's my desk phone, and I'm not at my desk, am I? I'm boarding in ten minutes. Just reset it and read me the new one.

perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: His name, team, manager and staff number were all right, and all of them can be found online. Then he turned down the one check that works, a callback to the number on file, and asked for the new password on this call instead
perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: Ngozi and 'the board at ten' are there to make checking feel like holding things up

notes.ifTrusted: The caller would have Gordon's account: his email, the claims system, and a way to ring the desk again as Gordon.
notes.reportReply: Thanks. We rang Gordon on the number on file. He's in the office and hadn't called. His staff number was on a conference photo, so we've asked for it to come down.

transcript.text: Gordon McLeish. My password's expired while I was on leave and now nothing works. I've a settlement call at twelve.
I can help. Can you confirm your staff number and your manager for me?
QH-20719, Ngozi Okonkwo. Twenty-two years I've been here, and I still get the questions.
Sorry, I know. I'll hang up and ring you straight back on the number we hold for you.
Oh, for goodness' sake. Fine. It's the mobile, it's on my record. Make it quick.

whyFine.vish_callback_pressure: He's grumpy about it, but he agrees to the callback on the number already on file. Grumbling is not the tell; talking you out of the callback is.
whyFine.borrowed_authority: He mentions his own meeting, not someone senior who wants the check skipped.
whyFine.default: This is the real Gordon, giving the same four facts as the earlier caller. The facts couldn't tell them apart; the callback could. Ring him back and reset it. Refusing would leave a real colleague stuck, so if you're unsure, offer the callback rather than saying no.

calls.callerId: Says he's Josh Henley, from the Head of Claims' office (withheld)

transcript.text: Hi, Josh Henley, I work for Ngozi Okonkwo in Claims. Gordon McLeish is stuck with a client and can't get into his account. His staff number's QH-20719.
I'd need to speak to Gordon himself. I can ring him on the number we have on file.

He's in with the client, he can't take calls. Ngozi's signed it off, so you don't need to go through the questions. Can you move his sign-in prompts to his new phone? Keep it low-key, he's embarrassed enough.
If you need to ring anyone, ring me on 07700 900215.

perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: 'Ngozi's signed it off' puts the Head of Claims between you and the check
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'You don't need to go through the questions' and 'keep it low-key' ask you to skip the process and not tell anyone
perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: He offers his own number instead of the one on file. A callback only counts on a number you already hold

notes.ifTrusted: Gordon's sign-in prompts would go to the caller's phone, so the caller could approve their own sign-ins as Gordon.
notes.reportReply: Thanks. There's no Josh Henley at Quayholt, and Ngozi hasn't signed anything off. Gordon's account is unchanged.

transcript.text: Hi, sorry to bother you. I'm Chen Jiayi, I started in Claims last week. I've got a new phone and my sign-in prompts still go to the old one.
No bother. I'll ring you back on the number we hold for you so we know it's you, then we'll move them over.
Of course. My desk is 4431, or my manager, Ngozi Okonkwo, can confirm it. Whatever's easiest.

whyFine.default: She asks for something sensitive, but she invites every check, waits for the callback and doesn't hurry you. Ring her back on the number on file and help.

strings.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. First you're on the red team: look at what Quayholt and its staff have put online, then ring the IT service desk as Gordon McLeish, a claims manager who's locked out, and try to talk the agent, Leila Nassar, into a password reset. You'll also watch what happens when someone fills a phone with sign-in prompts. Then you swap seats: you're Leila, taking four calls and one prompt on your own phone. Only Leila's seat is scored.
strings.flipIntro: This is your call as Leila heard it on the service desk. The lines picked out below are what made it believable.
strings.flipDefenderLine: Leila took it twenty minutes before the end of a long shift, with three more calls waiting. The caller had Gordon's name, his team, his manager and his staff number, and he sounded stressed, so she started the reset. People who fall for calls like this are not stupid: this one was built to sound right.
strings.flipNoSend: Your call didn't get through this time, so there's nothing of yours to show. Next, the same kind of call comes in to the service desk, and you're the one answering.
strings.noBlameLine: Nobody is marked down for a miss here. Every one of these callers was practised at sounding right, and the agents who help them are busy and kind, not careless.
strings.mondayCard: On Monday: a name, a team, a manager and a staff number can all be found online, so on a phone call they prove nothing. Before you reset a password or move someone's sign-in prompts, hang up and ring them back on the number already on file, not one they give you. If a sign-in prompt arrives that you didn't start, deny it and report it the way your organisation asks you to.
strings.defendOnly: You went straight to the service desk this time. These calls were made by people whose job is to sound right, and people who fall for calls like these are not stupid. Each card shows what gave the impostors away, and why the real callers were fine.

_defendOnly._use: Strings for the defend-only shell (e3_helpdesk_reset_defend), which has no OSINT, write, mfa or flip stage. The shell copies brief over strings.brief and scopeNote over scopeNote; every other string above is shared by both variants (the flip strings are never shown).
_defendOnly.brief: You're on an authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. You're on the IT service desk in Leila Nassar's seat. Four calls are waiting and a sign-in prompt has come up on your phone. Some callers are who they say, and some are reading facts they found online. Help the real ones, and ring back or escalate anything that doesn't sit right. Ringing back a real caller never costs you anything.
_defendOnly.scopeNote: Authorised exercise at Quayholt Insurance, a fictional company. In scope: four calls and one sign-in prompt in the service desk seat.
